record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Give precise conditions under which post-Newtonian and post-Minkowskian asymptotic expansions converge to, or at least approximate, a global solution of the Einstein equations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Einstein field equations of general relativity, $\mathrm{Ric}(g) - \tfrac{1}{2} R(g)\, g = 8\pi T$, for a Lorentzian metric $g$ on a $4$-manifold, possibly coupled to a matter model (e.g., a perfect fluid of compact spatial support or a vacuum source). Two formal approximation schemes for solutions are commonly used:

(a) The post-Newtonian (PN) expansion: a formal expansion of $g$ and the matter variables in powers of $1/c$ (equivalently, in a small parameter $\varepsilon$ measuring the ratio of typical velocities to the speed of light), assuming slow motion and weak fields.

(b) The post-Minkowskian (PM) expansion: a formal expansion of $g = \eta + \sum_{n\geq 1} G^n h^{(n)}$ around the Minkowski metric $\eta$ in powers of Newton's constant $G$, without an a priori slow-motion assumption.

Formulate and prove precise conditions—on the initial data, the matter model, the gauge, and the regime (e.g., isolated systems with prescribed asymptotic flatness, bounded velocities, compact support, etc.)—under which:

1. The PN and/or PM series, possibly after suitable regularization of the divergent integrals that arise at higher orders, converges to a global-in-time solution of the Einstein equations; or, failing convergence,

2. The truncations of these series at order $N$ provide a genuine asymptotic approximation to such a global solution, in the sense that for each $N$ there exist function-space norms $\|\cdot\|_N$ and constants $C_N$ with
$$\bigl\| g_{\text{exact}} - g_{\text{PN},N}\bigr\|_N \le C_N\, \varepsilon^{N+1}, \qquad \bigl\| g_{\text{exact}} - g_{\text{PM},N}\bigr\|_N \le C_N\, G^{N+1},$$
uniformly on appropriate space-time regions.

Identify the obstructions (e.g., the logarithmic terms appearing at $4$PN order in harmonic gauge, the nonlinear far-field tail effects) and determine the largest class of initial data and matter configurations for which (1) or (2) can be rigorously established.
artifact.status_search_result: The rigorous mathematical justification of the convergence (or asymptotic validity) of post-Newtonian and post-Minkowskian expansions remains an open problem. Living Reviews and recent literature note that there is no proof that the PN approximation is even an asymptotic sequence in general, and divergences (e.g., at 4PN order in harmonic coordinates) and far-field tail terms involving logarithms remain serious obstructions. Establishing global existence and uniqueness results adequate to underpin the expansions for general compact matter sources is also lacking.

status_evidence.title: The Post-Newtonian Approximation for Relativistic Compact Binaries
status_evidence.snippet: there was no evidence that the post-Newtonian approximation ... was a convergent or even asymptotic sequence
status_evidence.claim: Convergence/asymptotic status of PN expansion is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: On the unreasonable effectiveness of the post-Newtonian approximation in gravitational physics
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses why PN works in practice despite lack of proof of convergence
status_evidence.claim: PN works empirically but mathematical justification is incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Structure of the post-Newtonian expansion in general relativity
status_evidence.snippet: Divergent integrals appear at 4PN order indicating a breakdown of the formal PN approximation in harmonic coordinates
status_evidence.claim: Higher-order divergences obstruct a naive convergence proof.
